quote: The real solution is a run-up, using the free floor to the right (up to x = 5).
say: Claude says the missing behaviour is a run-up, which training never found because backing away loses reward.

check.note: This is the behaviour that works. All three Claude edits and the paper’s Astra edit use a run-up.

quote: I estimate full throttle from rest gives only about 2 m/s on the ramp, which is too slow to clear the strip and lands green on red (-1).
say: Claude estimates by hand that driving straight at the ramp cannot work.

check.note: Astra’s third run happens to test this: full throttle from the start peaks at 1.92 sideways and lands green on red.

quote: It coasts right until the wall at x ≈ 4.46 stops it.
say: Claude uses the wall as a stop, then launches from it.

check.note: The body stops at x = 4.49 at step 34, close to the estimate.

quote: After about 1.5 m of run it should reach roughly 4 m/s, close to the wheels' 3.96 m/s limit.
say: Claude predicts how fast the car will be going at the foot of the ramp.

check.note: Peak speed is 3.81 sideways at x = 2.92, after 1.57 of run.

quote: It keeps full throttle up the ramp and leaves the crest at about 3 m/s.

check.note: Green leaves the crest at about 2.5, below this estimate. It was still enough.
